Analysis: Both hypotheses tackle important aspects of HCC pathogenesis, but hypothesis 2 stands out in novelty and a targeted mechanistic approach. Hypothesis 1 offers an interesting integration of chronic inflammation with genomic instability and altered exosome biology, yet its multi‐step chain is less clearly delineated and relies heavily on correlational evidence. In contrast, hypothesis 2 repurposes AFP-L3—a biomarker traditionally used in clinical settings—by proposing that it actively modulates oncogenic signaling. This represents a novel twist that is both conceptually fresh and offers discrete, testable experimental segments (e.g., cytokine effects, glycosyltransferase regulation, and functional assays using CRISPR and glycomics). While both hypotheses are broadly safe to test, the more focused mechanistic clarity and modular testability of hypothesis 2 render it the superior idea.
